cards.q: Name the four Sportsman branches in the 2026 book.
cards.a: Recreation/utility, Touring, Sport, and Special Editions.
cards.why: Sportsman = straddle-seat ATV. A handlebar and straddle-seat layout distinguish it from side-by-sides. The 2026 book separates recreation/utility, Touring, Sport, and Special Editions. The MY27 sheet contains 500/600 names; the 2026 book contains 450/570 names. Keep the years separate.

cards.q: Are RANGER 1000 and RANGER XP 1000 the same model?
cards.a: No. They are distinct model lines, with different specifications and trim offerings.
cards.why: RANGER = utility side-by-side. 1000, XP 1000, XD 1500, and XP Kinetic are separate model lines. CREW identifies a longer passenger configuration; seat count depends on the platform. The 2026 book uses SP 570 in the mid-size range; the MY27 sheet lists RANGER 600.

cards.q: Which part of “RZR Pro XP 4 Ultimate” identifies the trim?
cards.a: Ultimate is the trim; Pro XP is the platform name and 4 identifies the four-seat configuration.
cards.why: RZR = sport side-by-side. Recognize Trail, Trail S, XP, XP S, Pro XP, Pro S, Pro R, and Pro R Boost as different names in the MY27 sheet. Platform name and Sport/Ultimate trim are separate parts of a model name. A 4-seat model and RZR 200 EFI youth model are distinct configurations.

cards.q: Does XP automatically mean more horsepower than GENERAL 1000 in the 2026 book?
cards.a: No. Both overview pages list 100 hp; width, suspension, tires, and ground clearance differ.
cards.why: GENERAL = crossover side-by-side. GENERAL 1000 and GENERAL XP 1000 are separate lines. The 2026 book lists 100 hp for both in its overview pages. The MY27 sheet lists GENERAL 1000 Sport and GENERAL XP Sport/Ultimate configurations.

cards.q: What is the quickest physical distinction between XP and ADV?
cards.a: XP has an open dumping cargo box; ADV has covered rear cargo space.
cards.why: XP = open box · ADV = covered cargo. XP has an open rear cargo box with dumping capability. ADV has covered pass-through rear cargo space and an enclosed locking tailgate. The 5 versions have rear seating; the exact rear-seat arrangement differs between XP and ADV.

cards.q: Name the two youth side-by-sides on the supplied MY27 sheet.
cards.why: Scrambler and youth are separate branches. The MY27 sheet lists Scrambler XP 1000 S. Youth ATV names include Outlaw 70 EFI, Outlaw 110 EFI, Sportsman 110 EFI, and Phoenix 200. Youth side-by-side names include RANGER 150 EFI and RZR 200 EFI.

cards.q: How is a stock number different from a model code?
cards.a: The stock number identifies a dealer unit; the model code identifies a catalog configuration.
cards.why: Year → family → platform → seats → trim → finish. Example: RANGER CREW XP 1000 NorthStar Ultimate identifies family, passenger configuration, platform, cab/trim, and equipment tier. Model codes identify exact catalog rows; a stock number identifies a dealer unit. A model number is not a complete specification and does not always equal engine displacement.

cards.q: Does every machine with “Cab” in its name necessarily have air conditioning?
cards.a: No. Read the exact model-year equipment list.
cards.why: EPS = electronic power steering. EPS means electronic power steering. Cab identifies an enclosure configuration; it alone does not establish air conditioning. The 2026 RANGER XP 1000 NorthStar Premium table explicitly includes heating and air conditioning.

cards.q: Is a 1,000-lb cargo-box rating the same as total vehicle payload?
cards.a: No. Cargo-box capacity and total vehicle payload are separate ratings.
cards.why: Three separate weight limits. Towing capacity concerns the trailer being pulled. Payload concerns weight carried by the vehicle, subject to the manual’s definition. A cargo-box limit is a separate limit for the box; it is not the entire vehicle payload.

cards.q: What does tritoon describe?
cards.why: Two tubes or three; then the exact package. Tube count is distinct from boat length and floorplan. Bennington is represented in the inventory. Capacity, engine rating, installed motor, and tube package belong to the exact boat configuration.

cards.q: Does a Bennington model name alone specify its complete motor and option package?
cards.a: No. The actual build sheet and dealer listing identify the equipped package.
cards.why: Series + length designation + floorplan. SX and R are different series labels. Similar length designations can have different seating and floorplans. The model name does not by itself identify every installed engine, tube package, or option.

cards.q: What part of the layout gives a bowrider its name?
cards.why: Bowrider = open seating in the bow. The bow layout distinguishes it from a closed-bow arrangement. Propulsion type and engine package must be identified separately. Hull dimensions, passenger capacity, and installed equipment are separate specifications.

cards.q: Does boat length tell you the exact deck layout?
cards.a: No. The model and floorplan determine the arrangement.
cards.why: Deck boat = broad, open deck layout. Hurricane is a deck-boat brand represented in the inventory. Deck layout, storage, and swim access vary by model. Overall length does not fully describe the hull, seating layout, or engine package.

cards.q: Name three components to identify on a bass boat.
cards.a: Examples: casting decks, livewells, rod storage, trolling motor, and electronics.
cards.why: Casting decks, livewells, rod storage. Caymas and Lowe fishing models appear in the dealer inventory. Key components include casting decks, livewells, rod storage, trolling motor, and electronics. Hull construction, engine, and installed electronics vary between models and units.

cards.q: Can two boats with the same hull model have different electronics?
cards.a: Yes. Installed packages can differ by stock number.
cards.why: Read the hull and model, not just the brand. Identify the exact model name. Console arrangement and storage are separate from motor horsepower. Installed trolling motor and electronics may differ between two examples of the same hull model.

cards.q: Name the four major components in the package memory hook.
cards.why: Hull + motor + trailer + rigging. The hull model is separate from the outboard model and horsepower. Trailer, electronics, trolling motor, and rigging belong to the equipped package. Base model specifications and installed equipment are not always identical.

cards.q: Is hull length the same as the length of a boat on its trailer?
cards.a: No. Trailer and equipment dimensions affect overall storage length.
cards.why: Length, capacity, and loaded weight differ. Use the capacity plate and exact manufacturer information for load and people limits. Loaded trailering weight includes the relevant boat, motor, trailer, fuel, and gear. Storage dimensions include the trailer and fitted equipment, not just hull length.

cards.q: Which identifiers do you record separately from the boat model?
cards.a: The exact outboard model, horsepower, shaft length, controls, start method, and trim arrangement.
cards.why: Mercury is the engine, not the hull. Identify exact engine model and horsepower. Shaft length, steering/control arrangement, start method, and trim configuration are separate fields. The installed engine must be compatible with the boat and its ratings.

cards.q: Are Pro XS and four-stroke mutually exclusive?
cards.a: No. Pro XS engines can be four-strokes.
cards.why: Engine cycle and product line can overlap. Pro XS engines can also be four-strokes. Horsepower alone does not establish engine weight, controls, or gearcase. Read the complete model and specification sheet.

cards.q: Does matching horsepower guarantee matching rigging?
cards.a: No. Shaft, steering, controls, and other installation requirements still matter.
cards.why: Installation dimensions and controls matter. Shaft length must match the boat’s installation requirements. Steering, controls, starting, and trim are separate configuration details. Two engines with equal horsepower may require different rigging.

cards.q: Can horsepower alone tell you the exact top speed?
cards.a: No. Hull, load, propeller, and setup also affect it.
cards.why: Hull + load + engine + propeller. Hull and loaded weight affect acceleration and speed. Propeller pitch and design must suit the engine’s operating range. Horsepower alone does not establish a universal top speed.

cards.q: Does a horsepower badge prove electric start or power trim?
cards.a: No. Those are separate configuration details.
cards.why: Small engines have distinct configurations. Read shaft length and control type. Electric start and power trim are separate features. Do not infer the entire configuration from horsepower or an abbreviated listing name.

cards.q: Is cutting width identical to the mower’s overall width?
cards.a: No. Overall width can include tires, deck housing, and discharge components.
cards.why: Different steering layouts. A tractor generally uses a steering wheel and front steering wheels. Zero-turn models commonly use independent rear-wheel control; steering systems vary by model. Cutting width, overall width, engine, and transmission are separate specifications.

cards.q: What deck and engine are listed for this XT1 LT42 reference?
cards.a: A 42-inch deck and Cub Cadet 547cc engine.
cards.why: XT1 = tractor · LT42 = 42-inch model. The referenced dealer listing specifies a 42-inch deck. It lists a Cub Cadet 547cc engine. It has a hydrostatic transmission; verify the exact model-year unit.

cards.q: What four specification fields distinguish similar mower names?
cards.a: Deck width, engine model, engine power, and transmission.
cards.why: CC 30, XT1, and Z-series are separate lines. CC 30 H and XT1 LT42 are different rider configurations. A Z-series model is distinct from an XT1 tractor. Record deck width, engine model, engine power, and transmission separately.

cards.q: Which two deck sizes appear in the Z 275X references?
cards.why: Model name + deck configuration. Indexed references include 48-inch and 54-inch decks. Those references list a 24 hp Kawasaki FR Series engine. Treat these as specific referenced listings, not a claim about every Husqvarna zero-turn.

cards.q: Does a larger deck automatically mean a commercial mower?
cards.a: No. Drivetrain, construction, and manufacturer duty classification also matter.
cards.why: Deck size is only one specification. Deck width alone does not define residential or commercial construction. Transmission type and rated use are separate from engine horsepower. Deck construction, spindles, frame, and service access are meaningful comparison fields.

cards.q: Does a tool-only package necessarily include a battery and charger?
cards.a: No. Package contents must be checked separately.
cards.why: Tool + power platform + attachment. Husqvarna and DeWalt are dealership brands identified in the earlier research. Tool model and battery platform are separate identifiers. Batteries, chargers, and attachments must match the exact product compatibility information.

cards.q: A 7,000-lb GVWR trailer weighs 2,000 lb empty. What is the approximate payload?
cards.a: 5,000 lb before considering any lower applicable limits.
cards.why: GVWR − empty weight = available payload. Approximate payload is GVWR minus empty trailer weight, subject to all other applicable ratings. Usable deck dimensions and ramp ratings are separate fields. Axle, tire, coupler, hitch, and towing limits must also be respected.

cards.q: What three vehicle identifiers come first in an accessory fit check?
cards.why: Year + model + trim + installation. An accessory for one model year may not fit another. Included equipment is different from an optional accessory. Mounting hardware and installation requirements are separate from the accessory’s name.

cards.q: What distinguishes two units with identical model names?
cards.a: Their stock numbers and actual installed equipment; color and location may also differ.
cards.why: Year → family → model → trim → equipment. Read the full model year and name. Identify the platform and trim before memorizing specifications. Use the stock number to distinguish individual units with the same model name.

cards.q: What is the difference between ground clearance and suspension travel?
cards.a: Ground clearance is the space beneath the vehicle; suspension travel is the wheel/suspension movement range.
cards.why: Rating + units + exact model year. Displacement in cc is different from horsepower. Ground clearance is different from suspension travel. MSRP is different from a dealer advertised price; both are dated references.
